definitions: A drug formerly used as a sedative and hypnotic, but withdrawn after it was found to cause severe birth defects.
A drug currently used in the treatment of certain cancers and other conditions, such as leprosy, due to its immunomodulatory and anti-angiogenic properties.
examples: The thalidomide tragedy led to stricter drug regulations.
Thalidomide is now used to treat multiple myeloma.
